state.case_summary:
A 29-year-old man from Tunisia presented with a two-month history of fever, weight loss, and chest pain during inhalation. He had experienced genital and oral ulcers over the past five months. On initial physical examination, his temperature was 38°C, and he had multiple pseudofolliculitis, as well as oral and scrotal ulcerations. Laboratory tests on admission showed a haemoglobin level of 13 g/dl, an erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 105 mm/hr, and a C-reactive protein concentration of 204 mg/l. Tests for antiphospholipid antibodies, protein C, protein S, and antithrombin III deficiencies were negative. The plasma total homocysteine level was 27 μmol/l (normal < 10 μmol/l). HLAB5 and pathergy tests were positive. An electrocardiogram indicated sinus rhythm tachycardia, and a chest X-ray was normal.

Transoesophageal echocardiography revealed a cardiac mass in the right atrium of 20/23 mm size attached into atrial septum protruding through the tricuspid valve into the right ventricle. CT scan showed a partial obstruction of the terminal portion of the inferior vena cava and thrombosis of the left lobar pulmonary artery with multiple pulmonary infarcts.
